messages:
alex: Heads-up — hit a weird case in canary where fallback fired but Console shows zero fallback events for that rollout. Seen this before?

karina: yeah, we've had gaps. runtime emits events but the Console UI only surfaces aggregated counts and sometimes filters out 'silent' fallbacks.

samir: can you paste the request id so I can trace? we log fallback details with event ids.

alex: req_01F2f8Qx — logs show `fallback=policy:model_capacity -> model-xsmall` around 13:41. Console only shows a 502 spike on the route, no fallback info.

bryan: that matches the product tradeoff: fewer noisy alerts in the Console. Operators want per-request linkage though.

karina: proposal: attach a small audit header on responses when a fallback happens, opt-in per-route. e.g.

```
X-Redwood-Fallback: latency.model_fallback
X-Redwood-Fallback-Event: fb_evt_20260321_0001
```

This gives operators a direct handle to fetch the full event payload for that request.

samir: nice UX, but careful about leaking internal heuristics in headers. Make it opt-in and only for internal keys. Also limit header contents to canonical tags, not stack dumps.

alex: agreed. header should be a single canonical tag + opaque event id. Console can use the id to call internal events API (authenticated).

deploy-bot: build #3412 deployed to canary. feature-flag: fallback-audit-header=true for canary routes. :rocket:

bryan: Console side: we should add a "Fallback timeline" view under Rollouts that shows ordered events and quick filters by rule, trigger type (latency/error/kvcache), and model variant. Click an event to see metadata + sampled input/response.

karina: telemetry schema additions: `fallback.rule`, `fallback.trigger`, `fallback.prev_model`, `fallback.latency_ms`, `route.policy_version`, `fallback.event_id`. Events should also have `sampled:true/false`.

samir: counterproposal: keep aggregated counters high-cardinality-free, emit sampled detailed events (1% default), and include only hashed user identifiers. Per-request headers ok for internal callers only. Also respect per-customer telemetry quotas — don't emit detailed events for every request on high-throughput routes.

alex: operational compromise: always emit aggregated increments (counts by rule/route/rollout), sampled detailed events at 1% (configurable per-org), and include the event id in a header when opted-in.

bryan: retention question — security/legal asked for 90 days of audit logs for fallback incidents. Ops pushed back on cost. Suggest default 30 days, enterprise opt-in for 365 days.

karina: decision candidate summarized: 1) runtime: add opt-in response header with canonical fallback tag + event id; 2) telemetry: aggregated counters always, sampled detailed events (default 1%); 3) Console: add Fallback timeline and event drilldown; 4) retention: 30d default, enterprise 365d opt-up; 5) feature-flag rollout behind `fallback-audit` and internal-only header exposure.

samir: action items: - runtime PR to attach header + event id (owner: samir) - telemetry schema PR (owner: karina) - Console wireframe + API integration (owner: bryan) - feature flag gating + docs (owner: alex)

alex: I'll write an RFC and a short rollout plan. tagging owners: @karina @samir @bryan. Thanks everyone — this should make operator debugging much less opaque. :+1:

bryan: small nit — also expose a quick KQL snippet in Console on the timeline: `fallback.event_id == "fb_evt_*" | sort timestamp desc | limit 50` so support can jump straight to logs.

karina: and add a mute/alerting policy: by default don't page on sampled events, only page on aggregate spike thresholds. ops can opt into per-event paging for critical customers.

alex: perfect. I'll include those in the RFC.
